**Finding: MISSING** — no IP/ownership clause exists in the Agreement.

**What I checked**
- §§1.1–1.3: HDI designs, develops, hosts and bears all costs of the Site — a classic deliverable, with no ownership statement.
- §1.4/1.5: HDI holds the system, admin tools and generates order export files; no data ownership language.
- §5.2/5.3: we get artistic/editorial control and "merchant of record" status, but control ≠ ownership.
- §6.1: we grant HDI a non-exclusive, limited, non-transferable licence in the Deerskin Marks solely to perform — properly narrow and in our favour, so not flagged.
- §8: Content, user information and data are treated only as Confidential Information (a use restriction, not title).
- §10.2 disclaims joint venture/co-ownership of the *relationship*, not of IP.
- Searches for "own", "intellectual property", "title", and a definition of "Content" turned up nothing on ownership or assignment.

**Why it fails the fallback**
There is no Customer ownership of deliverables, no HDI assignment, no Customer Data ownership sentence, and — critically — not even a licence-back of any HDI IP embedded in the Site. So neither the preferred nor the fallback position is met, despite our paying for the Site via the 30% Net Sales share and supplying the Content, Marks and all customer/order data.

**Redline (validated ok:true)** — new §5.5 inserted after §5.4:
- We own the Content, Marks, the Site and all deliverables/work product, plus all customer, order and transaction data ("Company Data"), with HDI assigning the same.
- HDI retains its pre-existing platform, tools and know-how, and grants us a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense any of it embedded in the Site.
- No assignment of our IP to HDI and no joint ownership.

This lands at the preferred position while expressly preserving HDI's platform ownership, so it should be an easy sell.
